study_guide.intro: Price Elasticity of Demand (PED) measures how responsive quantity demanded is to a change in price. It helps firms with pricing and governments with tax policy.
concept: Determinants: substitutes, necessity, time, income share.
Total revenue link: moving along a demand curve.
examples: Luxury fashion vs. salt (elastic vs. inelastic).
Fuel taxes and government revenue planning.
key_points: Sign convention: PED is negative; use absolute value for magnitude.
Elasticity varies along a linear demand curve.
Total revenue moves opposite to price when demand is elastic.

worked_example.answer: PED magnitude 0.4 → demand is inelastic; price ↑ raises total revenue.

mcq.stem: If |PED|=1.8, a price increase will likely…

saq.stem: Explain why PED tends to be higher in the long run.

laq.stem: ‘Indirect taxes on inelastic goods raise revenue but may be regressive.’ Evaluate.

notes: Total revenue test: elastic ↔ TR and P move opposite.
